[00:00] Coach (EN): Thank you for having me in your class today. I am here to support you, not to judge. Can we talk for a few minutes about the fractions lesson?

[00:08] Teacher (EN): Yes, of course. Thank you for coming.

[00:10] Coach (EN): Two things really worked. First, when a student gave an answer, you asked why, and waited, and she explained her reasoning about the shaded parts. That pushed the whole class to think.

[00:21] Teacher (EN): I was not sure if that was useful.

[00:24] Coach (EN): It was. Second, your definition of the numerator was very clear. You pointed at the shaded parts on the board and said, "The top number counts them," and the students repeated it correctly.

[00:35] Teacher (EN): Thank you. I practiced that explanation.

[00:38] Coach (EN): What did you notice about how many students were talking during the lesson?

[00:43] Teacher (EN): Honestly, mostly the same few students answered. The others were quiet.

[00:47] Coach (EN): That is a good observation. One thing to try next time: after you ask a question, give everyone 10 seconds to think. Then have them tell a partner before anyone answers. That way more students speak.

[01:01] Teacher (EN): I can try "think, pair, share" in the next fractions lesson.

[01:07] Coach (EN): Great. So your commitment is to use "think, pair, share" at least twice in your next lesson. I will come back in 2 weeks to see how it goes. Is that all right?

[01:17] Teacher (EN): Yes, that is fine.
